.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Remaining dry with above normal temperatures, 
then some rain possible late this week into early next week.

Clouds are still expected to trend downward in coverage 
slightly overnight, but there will still be passing clouds here 
and there. Cannot rule out a rogue sprinkle in the northern
Alleghenies. Overnight lows tonight will be in the 40s.

Upper ridging will build overhead tomorrow as high pressure
remains in place offshore. Dry conditions and above normal
temps are forecast beneath a mixture of clouds and sun. High 
temps will generally be in the lower to middle 70s, and winds 
will remain light out of the south. Patchy fog may be possible 
tomorrow night, with lows in the upper 40s to lower 50s.

Dry conditions and above normal temps will persist through the 
daylight hours on Wed. High temps will once again reach well 
into the 70s, and winds will begin to pick up slightly out of 
the south. Mostly sunny skies are expected to start the day, but
high clouds will be on the increase during the afternoon and 
evening hours in advance of an upper trough approaching from the
west. A sw embedded within the broader trough will lift 
northeastward through the Great Lakes Sun night. This system has
trended further northwest and a bit further away from the area,
but a few showers could still be possible by later Wed night.

The synoptic pattern across the eastern CONUS becomes much more 
active at the end of this week, through the weekend, and into early 
next week. A series of large upper troughs over the Midwest are 
forecast to steadily push north and east toward the Mid-Atlantic. 
One notable change over the last several model cycles is that the 
initial upper trough does not pass directly through our area, 
instead slides northeast across the OH Valley into PA. A weaker 
shortwave ahead of the main trough does cross our region Thu, 
and this lkly brings at least scattered showers and a few 
tstorms. However, given that the strongest upper level support 
now remains north of our area, we probably won't be getting a 
lot of precip like earlier models run depicted. Above normal 
temps lkly to end the week as highs reach the upper 60s to mid 
70s. More abundant cloud cover on Fri keeps temps a few degrees 
lower than Thu.

The secondary upper trough and an associated cold front dig into the 
Mid-Atlantic Fri afternoon into Fri night. However, it appears 
this second system will be rather progressive and models 
indicate the surface reflection "skipping" the Alleghenies, then
redeveloping east of I-95. If that occurs we'll see little 
precip outside of the mtns. Another hindering signal is models 
indicate a potential dry slot ahead of the cold front, which 
also cuts down on how much shower activity can develop. 

Most of the mid-level vorticity associated with this second upper 
trough cuts off over the central Great Lakes Fri night into 
Sat, then pushes well to our north/east Sun. Given the recent 
trends in the evolution of the synoptic pattern late this week, 
the NBM PoPs are lkly way too high for Thu and Fri. 

Looking ahead at Sunday into early next week, the active pattern 
brings another strong trough to the region Sun night into 
Mon. This system is forecast to be much larger than the 
previous two, and bring colder air in its wake. Periods of 
showers are possible at times on Mon, though model timing 
varies so this could change in the coming days.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions and light southerly winds will
continue through Wed. Some patchy fog could be possible in 
spots Tue night. Prevailing VFR conditions and southerly winds 
lkly continue into Thu, but showers or thunderstorms could lead 
to sub- VFR conditions at times. Winds are forecast to shift to 
out of the west on Fri, with a return to VFR conditions.

&&

.MARINE...
Sub-SCA level southerly winds are expected both today and
tomorrow with high pressure in place offshore. Winds will remain
out of the south for Wed and Thu, but gusts could near low-end 
SCA levels during that time. Sub-SCA conditions are expected to 
continue on Fri as winds shift to out of the west.
